summary.title: io_uring zero copy Rx
summary.one_liner: Learn how io_uring ZC Rx delivers packet payloads straight into userspace memory on header-split NICs, including the NIC setup with ethtool and the registration, receive, and buffer-recycling API steps.
takeaways: ZC Rx requires a NIC with header/data split, flow steering, and RSS so payloads land in userspace while headers still go through the kernel TCP stack.
NIC configuration (ethtool -L, -G tcp-data-split, -X, -N) is done out of band and is not configured by the kernel API.
Setup needs an io_uring instance with SINGLE_ISSUER, DEFER_TASKRUN, and CQE32 or CQE_MIXED flags, plus an mmap'd memory area and refill ring.
Buffers are returned to the kernel by writing struct io_uring_zcrx_rqe entries to the refill ring and advancing the tail.
rx_buf_len can hint larger chunk sizes, falling back to zero (page size) if registration fails.
summary.summary: This kernel documentation page describes io_uring zero copy Rx (ZC Rx), which receives packet data directly into user memory without kernel-to-user copies, unlike TCP_ZEROCOPY_RECEIVE and kernel-bypass stacks such as DPDK. It lists the required NIC features (header/data split, flow steering, RSS) and gives the ethtool commands used to set them up. It then walks through the low-level io_uring API: creating the ring, mapping a memory area and refill ring, registering the interface queue, submitting multishot IORING_OP_RECV_ZC requests, processing CQEs, and recycling buffers. The page ends with notes on area chunking via rx_buf_len and a pointer to the kernel selftest.
